title: Mechanical Characterization of Aluminum Silicate (Al 2 SiO 5 )/Alumina (Al 2 O 3 )-Reinforced Al6082 Hybrid Metal Matrix Composites: Monotonic Tensile Strength, Fatigue, and Fractographic Investigation
abstract: Abstract Particulate-reinforced metal matrix composites (MMCs) are gaining significant importance in advanced materials research due to their superior mechanical properties and also suitability for structural applications under monotonic and cyclic loading conditions. However, limited studies reported the combined experimental and numerical investigation of monotonic tensile behavior, high-cycle fatigue life, fatigue crack propagation, and fractographic characteristics of Al6082-based hybrid MMCs reinforced with dual ceramic particulates. The present work addresses this gap by investigating the mechanical behavior of Al6082 hybrid MMCs reinforced with alumina (Al 2 O 3 ) and aluminum silicate (Al 2 SiO 5 ), synthesized using the stir-casting process. The influence of material composition and the process parameters on microstructure, tensile strength, fatigue life, and fracture behavior is systematically examined for different Al 2 O 3  contents while maintaining Al 2 SiO 5  at a constant 5 wt.%. A maximum tensile strength of 198 N/mm 2  was achieved for the composite containing 5 wt.% Al 2 SiO 5  and 10 wt.% Al 2 O 3 , representing a significant improvement compared to the unreinforced Al6082 alloy and aluminum-based MMCs reported in the literature. The composites with 10-15 wt.% Al 2 O 3  exhibited enhanced fatigue and fatigue crack propagation life in the range of 8.4 × 10 6  to 1.11 × 10 7  cycles, attributed to improved load transfer, grain refinement, and strong interfacial bonding. Fractographic analysis under monotonic and cyclic loading conditions provides valuable insights into the dominant failure mechanisms and the role of ceramic reinforcements in governing crack initiation and propagation. The outcomes of this study demonstrate the potential of Al6082/Al 2 O 3 /Al 2 SiO 5  hybrid MMCs for fatigue-critical structural applications.
journal: Journal of Materials Engineering and Performance

sections.heading: Introduction
paragraphs: Aluminum (Al) alloys and its composites offer numerous advantages across various industries, as these are lightweight, making them ideal for applications where weight reduction is crucial in aerospace structures such as fuselages, wings, and interior components (Ref  1 ,  2 ). Al alloys exhibit natural corrosion resistance, reducing maintenance needs and increasing durability. This property is beneficial in marine and architectural applications. They also possess excellent thermal conductivity and good electrical conductivity, making them suitable for heat exchangers and cooling systems in electronics and automotive industries, and potentially in electrical transmission lines (Ref  3 ,  4 ).

Aluminum-based metal matrix composites (MMCs) have garnered significant attention due to their promising monotonic and fatigue properties. Studies show that MMCs, reinforced with materials like silicon carbide (SiC) or titanium diboride (TiB 2 ), exhibit improved monotonic tensile strength, elongation, and hardness compared to traditional Al alloys (Ref  5 ,  6 - 7 ). Additionally, research highlights the enhanced fatigue behavior of these composites, with fatigue life and fatigue strength being notably improved (Ref  8 ). Investigations on in situ TiB 2 /7050Al MMCs reveal insights into fatigue mechanisms, stress concentration, and fatigue life, indicating their suitability for fatigue-critical applications (Ref  8 ). The electrical conductivity, magnetic, and fatigue properties of Al matrix composites make them desirable for structural applications requiring high specific strength and wear resistance (Ref  9 ,  10 - 11 ). Overall, the combination of enhanced monotonic and fatigue properties positions Al-based MMCs as promising materials for various industrial applications (Ref  12 ,  13 ).

In recent years, considerable work has been carried out on the mechanical and tribological properties of aluminum-based MMCs. Premnath et al. (Ref  14 ) reported a 33% increase in the surface hardness of alumina (Al 2 O 3 )-reinforced aluminum MMCs with an increase in Al 2 O 3  concentration from 5% to 15%. Kim et al. (Ref  15 ) observed that addition of particles up to a volume fraction around 15-20% resulted in a significant improvement in the yield stress, ultimate tensile strength, and fracture strain of the aluminum-based MMCs under monotonic loading, whereas further addition of reinforcements caused a reduction in these properties. Similar observations have been made by other works, which show a limit of around 15% of particulate volume fraction, beyond which the mechanical and physical properties deteriorate (Ref  16 ). Bommanna et al. (Ref  17 ) assessed the strength and elongation behavior of SiC- and B 4 C-reinforced AA6061 hybrid composite. Vijayakumar et al. (Ref  18 ) analyzed the tensile strength, hardness, and porosity of ZrSiO 4 /TiC-reinforced Al6082.

Several recent studies demonstrate how particulate reinforcements can significantly alter key performance parameters in aluminum alloys. For example, Kumar et al. ,  (Ref  19 ) investigated Al7075 composites reinforced with ZrO 2  and graphite particulates ,  reporting notable improvements in tensile strength and wear resistance. Results revealed the complex interplay between reinforcement type and mechanical response. Similarly, Ahmad et al. (Ref  20 ) studied Si 3 N 4 /ZrO 2  hybrid reinforcement in heat-treated Al7055 MMCs ,  showing that proper dispersion and heat treatment processing can lead to substantial enhancements in both microstructural characteristics and wear behavior. Ravikumar et al. (Ref  21 ) investigated Al7075 reinforced with nanoscale SiC-graphite using the stir-casting technique, focusing on its microstructural and mechanical characteristics. The study reported a uniform distribution of the reinforcements within the aluminum matrix, leading to improved mechanical properties with the incorporation of SiC particles. However, the addition of solid lubricants such as graphite, in combination with hard ceramic particulates, resulted in a reduction in the overall strength of the hybrid composites.

Investigations carried out emphasized the significant role of reinforcement type, processing route, and interfacial bonding on the mechanical and fracture behavior of MMC. Investigations on aluminum-based composites have shown that the incorporation of ceramic reinforcements improves strength and hardness, while the resulting fracture mechanisms are driven by particle distribution, matrix-reinforcement adhesion, and the presence of defects or porosity (Ref  22 ). In particular, boron carbide-reinforced aluminum composites exhibit significantly enhanced mechanical strength and wear resistance, making them promising candidates for lightweight and high-performance structural applications (Ref  23 ). Detailed fractographic analyses further revealed that crack initiation and propagation are strongly influenced by the uniformity of reinforcement and the effectiveness of load transfer across the interface, leading to mixed mode fracture features under tensile loading (Ref  24 ). Moreover, the selection of fabrication technique plays a crucial role in determining microstructural refinement and overall mechanical response, as optimized processing conditions contribute to enhanced densification and reduced agglomeration of reinforcement particles (Ref  25 ). Similar observations have been reported for hybrid and particulate reinforced systems, in which improved mechanical performance is associated with refined grain structure, homogeneous reinforcement distribution, and strong interfacial characteristics (Ref  26 ). Therefore, these findings collectively highlight the importance of microstructural control and processing optimization for achieving superior mechanical properties and reliable fracture performance in advanced composite materials.

A critical review on the existing literature indicates that most investigations on aluminum-based MMCs have primarily focused on monotonic mechanical properties such as tensile strength, hardness, and wear behavior, often considering single ceramic reinforcements or limited hybrid systems. Although a few studies have addressed the fatigue performance of Al-based MMCs, these are generally restricted to S-N fatigue behavior, with limited emphasis on fatigue crack propagation and detailed fracture mechanism analysis. Furthermore, comprehensive studies that simultaneously correlate microstructural characteristics, monotonic tensile response, high-cycle fatigue life, fatigue crack propagation behavior, and numerical validation, particularly for Al6082-based hybrid MMCs reinforced with Al 2 SiO 5  and Al 2 O 3  remain scarce. Consequently, the combined influence of dual ceramic reinforcements and stir-casting process parameters on fatigue and fracture behavior is not yet well understood. In this context, the present work addresses these gaps by providing an integrated experimental and numerical investigation, identifying the optimal reinforcement content, and establishing clear microstructure–property–failure relationships for fatigue-critical structural applications.

Thus, the objective of the present work is to investigate the static strength, fatigue strength, and fracture resistance of aluminum-based MMCs with the addition of aluminum silicate (Al 2 SiO 5 ) and alumina (Al 2 O 3 ) as particulate reinforcements. The matrix chosen is Al6XXX series-based aluminum 6082 alloy whose main alloying elements are magnesium, manganese, and silicon with some traces of tin, zinc, and chromium. Ceramic reinforcements were chosen to reinforce the Al7075 and Al6082 alloy based upon their outstanding properties like high hardness, compressive strength, fracture toughness, and high temperature resistance (Ref  27 ,  28 ). The prepared composite specimens are initially subjected to density analysis and microstructural investigations using SEM. This is followed by the monotonic tensile tests coupled with fractographic analysis of the fractured samples. The fatigue and fracture resistance behaviors of the composites are examined through experimental tests and numerical simulations. Also, the corresponding failed specimens are examined to understand the failure mechanisms in action during the different loading conditions. A Taguchi-based design of experiments approach is utilized to assess the impact of material composition and stir-casting process parameters on the mechanical properties of the MMCs. Analysis of variance (ANOVA) is used to determine the statistical significance of the process parameters.

sections.heading: Composite Preparation
paragraphs: The material for the matrix in present work is Al6082. The chemical composition of the matrix material was analyzed using x-ray fluorescence (XRF). The results of XRF test for the three types of hybrid composites prepared with different wt. % of Al 2 O 3  particles are provided in Appendix 1. The composite was prepared by adding Al 2 O 3  (5%, 10%, and 15% of total weight) and Al 2 SiO 5  (kept constant at 5%) particles of size 30 µm and 50 µm as reinforcement to Al6082 matrix. Initially, Al6082 ingots were placed inside a graphite crucible superheated to 750 °C. The molten metal was degassed using Hexachloroethane (C 2 C1 6 ) tablets. Subsequently, reinforcements were added with different stirring speed and time durations. Figure  1  shows the stir-casting unit, and the zirconium-coated steel mechanical stirrer used for fabrication of hybrid composites, which avoids the possibility of reaction between the molten metal and stirrer. The reinforcements were added in sequence, i.e., first the Al 2 SiO 5  particles were added followed by the addition of Al 2 O 3  particles. The addition of ceramic particles was gradual to prevent formation of clusters and ensure good dispersion in the molten metal. After completing the mixing process, the molten metal is immediately poured into the preheated rectangular shaped permanent mold made of cast iron. Table  1  shows the levels of process parameters considered for the investigations. The experimental plan is made using the Taguchi’s L 9  orthogonal array design. Table  2  presents the detailed information on the design of experiments. sections.heading: Microstructural Characterization and Density Analysis
paragraphs: The microstructural characteristics of the prepared MMC specimens are analyzed using SEM (FESEM, ZEISS Sigma 300, Carl Zeiss, Germany) equipped with an energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy (EDS) detector. SEM analysis was carried out to evaluate the dispersion of reinforcement particles, grain morphology, intermetallic phases, and fracture features at both low and high magnifications. Elemental composition and phase distribution within the matrix and reinforcement regions were confirmed using EDS analysis.

Density of the different compositions of Al6082/Al 2 SiO 5 /Al 2 O 3  hybrid MMCs is analyzed by means of the Archimedes principle. An analytical balance with an accuracy of ± 0.001 g was used to measure the mass of the specimens, while a graduated measuring cylinder was used to determine the displaced water volume. The density was calculated as the ratio of measured mass to the corresponding volume of each specimen.

sections.heading: Monotonic/Cyclic Strength Characterization and Fractographic Analysis
paragraphs: Monotonic tensile tests were carried out in accordance with ASTM E8 standards using a universal testing machine (BISS 25 kN, Bangalore Integrated System Solutions Pvt. Ltd., India) (refer Fig.  2 ). The tests were conducted at room temperature to determine the tensile strength and deformation behavior of the hybrid composites. Fig. 2 (a) Schematic showing the dimensions of the tensile test specimen and (b) photographs of the prepared aluminum composite specimens used for tensile testing

Resistance to cyclic loading and crack propagation, known as fracture toughness, is an important aspect to understand and prevent catastrophic failures of critical components in several applications. Particularly in case of composites reinforced with particulates, it is very important to assess the nature of crack propagation and crack blunting under the presence of hard ceramic reinforcements in the soft ductile matrix. Accordingly, the effects of stir-casting parameters (stirring speed and duration) and Al 2 O 3  weight percentage on fatigue crack propagation behavior were investigated.

High-cycle fatigue tests were also performed using the same BISS 25 kN servo-hydraulic testing system under load-controlled conditions. The tests were conducted at room temperature using a sinusoidal loading waveform. The dimensions of the fatigue and crack propagation specimens are shown in Fig.  3 . Fig. 3 Schematic showing the dimensions of (a) high-cycle fatigue and (b) fracture crack propagation test specimen

Fractographic analysis of tensile- and fatigue-fractured specimens is performed using a field-emission scanning electron microscope (ZEISS Sigma 300, Carl Zeiss, Germany) to identify dominant fracture mechanisms, crack initiation sites, particle fracture, and interfacial failure characteristics.

sections.heading: Microstructural Investigation
paragraphs: Figure  4  shows the SEM micrographs of the Al6082 hybrid composite obtained with different processing parameters such as different Al 2 O 3  particle contents, stirring rates, and mixing times. From the figure, it can be seen that the microstructure consists of dendrites composed of α-aluminum, intermetallic compounds, and reinforcements in the inter-dendritic spaces. From Fig.  4 (c), it is observed that the aluminum grain size for α-B5 sample is smaller than other hybrid composite samples (B1, B3, and B7). However, the distribution of Al 2 O 3  and Al 2 SiO 5  particles is not clear from low-magnification micrographs. Fig. 4 Low-magnification SEM micrographs of Al6082/Al 2 SiO 5 /Al 2 O 3  hybrid MMCs fabricated under different processing conditions: (a) 5 wt.% Al 2 O 3 , 150 rpm, 5 min; (b) 5 wt.% Al 2 O 3 , 250 rpm, 15 min; (c) 10 wt.% Al 2 O 3 , 200 rpm, 15 min; and (d) 15 wt.% Al 2 O 3 , 150 rpm, 15 min, showing the overall matrix morphology and inter-dendritic microstructural features

Several high-magnification micrographs of sample B5 were taken to examine the particle distribution and their association with the matrix, as depicted in Fig.  5 (a) for the Al6082 hybrid composite containing 5% Al 2 SiO 5  and 10% Al 2 O 3  particles, with a mixing duration of 15 minutes at a speed of 200 rpm. The microstructure comprises α-Al and Al 2 O 3  particles within α-Al grains as the primary phase. It is found that only Al 2 O 3  particles are packed inside the grain and very well connected with the matrix, whereas Al 2 SiO 5  particles are not visible due to the low content. Dispersion of Al 2 O 3  particles is uniform throughout the matrix with good interfacial bonding. This is very important because only a good dispersion of reinforcement can yield better properties. The chemical composition of sample B5 was investigated using energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy (EDS), and the obtained spectrum is shown in Fig.  5 (b). EDS shows that Al6082 alloy contains main alloying elements such as Al, Mn, Fe, Si, and O associated with Al 2 O 3  and Al 2 SiO 5  particles. Figure  6  shows the presence of α-AlMnFeSi intermetallic compound that occupies the inter-dendritic space together with the reinforcements. EDS analysis of one of the inter-dendritic spaces shows the presence of the corresponding main elements. Fig. 5 (a) High-magnification SEM micrographs of B5 with 10% Al 2 O 3 , 200 rpm stirring speed, 15 min stirring time and (b) EDS results of Al6082/Al 2 SiO 5 /Al 2 O 3  hybrid MMCs Fig. 6 The B1 sample’s SEM and EDS data indicating the α-AlMnFeSi intermetallic compound

sections.heading: Density Analysis
paragraphs:
Density analysis of the Al6082/Al 2 SiO 5 /Al 2 O 3  hybrid composite systems is presented in Table  3 . It is observed that the addition of 5 wt.% Al 2 O 3  along with 5 wt.% Al 2 SiO 5  results in a hybrid composite density of 2.72 g/cm 3 , which is marginally higher than that of the unreinforced Al6082 alloy (2.71 g/cm 3 ). With a further increase in Al 2 O 3  content to 10 wt.% and 15 wt.%, the density increases to 2.78 g/cm 3  and 2.81 g/cm 3 , respectively. This gradual increase in density is attributed to the higher intrinsic densities of the ceramic reinforcements, namely Al 2 SiO 5  (3.13-3.17 g/cm 3 ) (Ref  16 ,  29 ) and Al 2 O 3  (3.98 g/cm 3 ) (Ref  30 ), compared to the Al6082 matrix.
 Table 3 Density of Al6082/Al 2 SiO 5 /Al 2 O 3  hybrid composite system Sample Mass, gm Initial volume of water in measuring cylinder, ml Final Volume of water in measuring cylinder, ml Change in volume, ml or cc Density, gm/cc 5% Al 2 O 3 14.43 29.7 35.0 5.3 2.7227 10% Al 2 O 3 13.10 29.3 34.0 4.7 2.7872 15% Al 2 O 3 12.66 32.0 36.5 4.5 2.8124

To assess the expected density variation with reinforcement content, the theoretical density of the hybrid composites was estimated using the rule of mixtures. Based on the densities of Al6082, Al 2 SiO 5 , and Al 2 O 3 , the calculated theoretical densities were approximately 2.78 g/cm 3 , 2.85 g/cm 3 , and 2.92 g/cm 3  for composites containing 5 wt.%, 10 wt.%, and 15 wt.% Al 2 O 3 , respectively, while maintaining Al 2 SiO 5  at a constant 5 wt.%. The experimentally measured densities are consistently lower than these theoretical values. This deviation can be attributed to micro-shrinkage porosity and localized particle clustering inherent to the stir-casting process, particularly at higher reinforcement contents. During solidification, particle agglomeration can hinder complete matrix infiltration between adjacent reinforcements, leading to discontinuities at the particle–matrix interface and the formation of micro-porosity. Such casting-induced porosity not only reduces the effective density of the composites but also influences their mechanical and physical properties. Similar reductions in experimental density relative to theoretical predictions have been widely reported for aluminum-based hybrid MMCs fabricated via stir casting, including systems reinforced with rice husk ash and SiC particles (Ref  31 ), and are consistent with the present microstructural observations.

By serving as stress concentrators, microporosities in hybrid composites impair their mechanical and physical characteristics by decreasing stiffness, fracture toughness, compressive strength, tensile strength, and crack propagation during fatigue loading. They reduce the hybrid structure’s enhanced strength by breaking the interfacial link between the reinforcements and matrix. Microporosities can cause long-term damage by physically reducing density, increasing moisture absorption, and decreasing thermal conductivity. The homogeneity and performance of the composite are compromised by these voids; thus, careful production methods are necessary to reduce their presence and guarantee the mechanical integrity and longevity of the composite. These micro-shrinkage pores reduce the effective load-bearing cross section and act as stress concentrators, thereby degrading tensile strength and promoting early crack initiation under both monotonic and cyclic loading. As a result, the strengthening effect of increased reinforcement content is partially offset at higher Al 2 O 3  levels.

sections.heading: Monotonic Tensile Strength Analysis
paragraphs:
Table  4  shows the value of peak tensile strengths obtained for Al6082/Al 2 SiO 5 /Al 2 O 3  hybrid composite systems with different combinations of weight percentage of Al 2 O 3  particles, stirring time, speed, and S/N ratio. Here, the weight percentage of Al 2 SiO 5  particles is fixed to 5 wt.% for every case from B1 to B9. For each composite composition, three tensile specimens were tested to ensure repeatability of the results. The tensile strength values reported in Table  4  represent the average of the three measurements obtained for each composition. Although standard deviations or error bars are not explicitly reported, the variation among the tested specimens for each composition was minimal, and consistent trends in tensile strength were observed across all tests. This repeatability supports the reliability of the reported tensile strength values and the comparative assessment of reinforcement content on mechanical performance (Table  5 ).
 Table 4 Tensile strength and corresponding S/N ratios of Al6082/Al 2 SiO 5 /Al 2 O 3  hybrid MMCs Specimen Wt. % Stir speed, rpm Stir Time, min Tensile strength, N/mm 2 S/N ratio B1 5 150 5 148.89 43.4573 B2 5 200 10 166.78 44.4429 B3 5 250 15 171.72 44.6964 B4 10 150 10 174.06 44.8140 B5 10 200 15 194.12 45.7614 B6 10 250 5 198.04 45.9351 B7 15 150 15 187.62 45.4656 B8 15 200 5 176.34 44.9270 B9 15 250 10 181.15 45.1608 Table 5 Mean S/N ratio for tensile strength hybrid composite system Level Wt.% Stir speed Stir time 1 44.20 44.58 44.77 2 45.50 45.04 44.81 3 45.18 45.26 45.31 Delta 1.30 0.69 0.53 Rank 1 2 3

It is observed that the tensile strength of Al6082 hybrid composite increased when the weight percentage of Al 2 O 3  is increased from 5% to 10 wt.%. However, when the weight percentage reached 15 wt.%, the tensile strength tends to decrease. Although the tensile strength increases significantly from 5 wt.% to 10 wt.% Al 2 O 3 , the difference between 10 wt.% and 15 wt.% Al 2 O 3  is comparatively small and does not represent a statistically meaningful improvement, as evidenced by the overlap in tensile strength values reported in Table  4 . The hybrid composite containing 10 wt.% Al 2 O 3  exhibited the highest tensile strength of 198.04 MPa, whereas the lowest value of 148.89 MPa was recorded for the composite with 5 wt.% Al 2 O 3 . This corresponds to an approximately 34.94% increase in tensile strength for the 10 wt.% Al 2 O 3 -reinforced hybrid composite compared to the 5 wt.% counterpart. This increase in tensile strength with increasing content of Al 2 O 3  particles can be attributed to the better load distribution and thereby greater stress bearing capability in the hybrid composite. This can be caused by several factors such as a decrease in grain size and an increase in density (Ref  32 ,  33 ). At 15 wt.% Al 2 O 3 , increased melt viscosity during stir casting promotes particle agglomeration and micro-porosity, which act as stress concentrators and offset the strengthening gained from additional reinforcement. The maximum tensile strength obtained in this work is comparable to the 190 N/mm 2  attained by (Ref  34 ) and (Ref  35 ) for purely Al 2 O 3 -based and fly ash/Al 2 O 3 -reinforced aluminum-based MMCs, respectively.

The incorporation of Al 2 O 3  and Al 2 SiO 5  particles significantly influences the microstructure of the Al6082 matrix by promoting grain refinement, increasing dislocation density, and inducing higher levels of plastic strain, which collectively affect the tensile strength of the hybrid composites. With increasing Al 2 O 3  weight fraction, the matrix grain size decreases due to two primary mechanisms: the provision of additional nucleation sites for new grains and the restriction of grain growth. During processing, Al 2 O 3  and Al 2 SiO 5  particles facilitate grain nucleation, while their uniform dispersion within the matrix impedes grain growth. Consequently, the Al6082 hybrid composite containing 10 wt.% Al 2 O 3  exhibits finer grains than the composite with 5 wt.% Al 2 O 3 . However, at higher reinforcement levels (15 wt.% Al 2 O 3 ), particle agglomeration during processing may occur, which disrupts effective grain refinement and leads to a comparatively lower tensile strength than that of the other composites.

Another significant strengthening mechanism arises from enhanced dislocation plasticity induced by the addition of Al 2 O 3  and Al 2 SiO 5  particles (Ref  36 ). When these reinforcements are introduced into the Al6082 matrix, the mismatch in elastic and plastic properties generates stress concentrations at the particle–matrix interfaces during tensile loading. To maintain displacement compatibility under applied stress, interfacial displacements are produced, leading to interactions between moving dislocations and the Al 2 O 3  and Al 2 SiO 5  particles. These dislocation–particle interactions play a crucial role in governing the strength of the hybrid composites and should be distinguished from strengthening associated with particle-stimulated nucleation during processing. Furthermore, the substantial mismatch in coefficients of thermal expansion between the Al6082 matrix (~ 23.4 × 10 -6 /K) and the Al 2 O 3  (~ 8.1 × 10 -6 /K) and Al 2 SiO 5  (~ 5.2 × 10 -6 /K) reinforcements results in the generation of thermally induced dislocations within the matrix. As the Al 2 O 3  weight fraction increases, the dislocation density correspondingly rises, which contributes positively to the enhancement of tensile strength in the hybrid composites. Figure  7  illustrates the mean effect of the processing parameters on the tensile strength of the hybrid MMCs. Fig. 7 Main effects plot for S/N ratio

In the presently developed hybrid MMCs, the strengthening mechanism is mainly dependent on Al 2 O 3 , Al 2 SiO 5  particles and the Al6082 matrix interface. Transferring the load from the matrix to the reinforcements is very important from the standpoint of interfacial load transfer (Ref  37 ). Due to the good bonding between the Al6082 matrix and the Al 2 O 3 /Al 2 SiO 5  particles, the interface is strong and sufficient to transfer the load from the matrix to the particulates during tensile loading. However, it should be noted that this is mostly dependent on the even dispersion of Al 2 O 3  particles in the Al6082 matrix. From the values, it is clear that Al 2 O 3  particle dispersion is uniform for Al6082 hybrid composites with 10 wt.% leading to higher strength values. However, with increasing content of Al 2 O 3  particles up to 15 wt.%, the tensile strength showed a decreasing trend.

The reduction in tensile strength observed for the hybrid composite containing 15 wt.% Al 2 O 3  can be attributed to microstructural factors associated with higher reinforcement content in stir-cast MMCs. SEM micrographs reveal localized particle clustering and an increased presence of micro-shrinkage porosity at higher Al 2 O 3  levels, which arise due to increased melt viscosity and reduced wettability during processing. These microstructural heterogeneities act as stress concentrators and promote premature crack initiation under tensile loading. Furthermore, particle agglomeration limits effective load transfer from the Al6082 matrix to the ceramic reinforcements and locally weakens the matrix–particle interface. As a result, the strengthening benefits gained from increased ceramic content are offset by porosity-induced damage and interfacial discontinuities, leading to a net reduction in tensile strength at 15 wt.% Al 2 O 3 . Similar reductions in tensile strength at elevated reinforcement contents have been widely reported for aluminum-based hybrid MMCs fabricated using liquid metallurgy routes.

Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) were used to confirm the uniform dispersion of Al 2 O 3  and Al 2 SiO 5  particles in the Al6082 matrix. This allowed for a better understanding of the distribution and elemental composition of the reinforcements within the matrix. Stir casting with ideal stirring parameters (e.g., speed, duration, and temperature) is used and mitigate the impacts of particle agglomeration, particularly at greater reinforcement content. Tensile testing was also carried out to evaluate the effect of agglomeration on mechanical characteristics; findings were compared with microstructural observations.

sections.heading: Fractographic Investigation of Monotonic Tensile Specimens
paragraphs: Figure  8 (a)-(h) shows the SEM micrographs of Al6082/Al 2 SiO 5 /Al 2 O 3  hybrid composite system with different weight percentages of Al 2 O 3  particles obtained after tensile test. SEM images of fractured hybrid composite specimens B1, B3, B5, and B7 in low and high magnifications are obtained to understand the failure mechanisms. As shown in Fig.  8 (a) and (c),  B1  and  B3  hybrid composite samples are found to fail in fiber variety, but they also showed some areas of dendritic regions. Particularly in case of sample B3, a big crack running into several microns is clearly visible in SEM micrograph as shown in Fig.  8 (c). As mentioned earlier, these cracks nucleate from micro-shrinkages which are the last regions to solidify where no molten metal can reach these inter-dendritic regions (Ref  38 ,  39 ). Due to insufficient molten metal flow into the inter-dendritic regions, the cracks are nucleated which tends to grow at a rapid pace when such samples are subjected to tensile loading. A magnified image of these hybrid composite samples shown in Fig.  8 (b) and 8(d) demonstrates the failure in ductile manner microscopically. But the most dominant mechanism for failure in these hybrid composite samples with low Al 2 O 3  particle content of 5 wt.% is inter-dendritic cracking. Further samples with high Al 2 O 3  particle content of 10 and 15 wt.% showed brittle type of fracture as shown in Fig.  8 (e) and (g). Some regions of particle fracture were seen for both B5 and B7 hybrid composite samples indicating good interfacial bonding between Al 2 O 3  and Al6082 matrix. Due to such good bonding, the tensile strength of hybrid composite samples B4 to B7 is comparatively higher than that of B1 to B3. Particularly, it can be attributed to the optimum processing parameters leading to good interfacial bonding. Further the extent of inter-dendritic cracking was very less in these hybrid composite samples (B5 and B7) which is mainly attributed to grain refinement. With an increase in Al 2 O 3  content to 10 and 15 wt.%, the grain size tends to decrease which improves the microstructure by forming more equiaxed fine sized grains. These fine grains provide utmost resistance to the crack formation at the solidification leading to minimal micro-shrinkage regions (Ref  40 ,  41 ). This is the reason for lack of such inter-dendritic cracking or micro-shrinkage regions in Fig.  8 (e)-(h). Fig. 8 Low- and high-magnification SEM images of tensile-fractured Al6082/Al 2 SiO 5 /Al 2 O 3  hybrid composites: (a, c, e, g) low and (b, d, f, h) high magnifications

The transition from ductile-to-brittle fracture with increasing Al 2 O 3  content from 5% to 15% weight was quantitatively analyzed using tensile testing to measure mechanical properties like elongation at break and fracture toughness, alongside fractographic analysis through scanning electron microscopy (SEM) to examine fracture surfaces. The findings demonstrated that as the Al 2 O 3  concentration increased, ductility decreased and brittle fracture characteristics such as cleavage facets and intergranular cracking increased. By encouraging a consistent grain structure, grain refinement achieved by the pinning action of tiny Al 2 O 3  particles helped increase strength and decrease micro-shrinkage. Furthermore, by strengthening load transfer and avoiding void formation at the matrix-reinforcement interface, better interfacial bonding between the Al 2 O 3  particles and the Al6082 matrix reduced crack propagation and partially offset the brittleness brought on by a higher particle content.

To ensure the representativeness of the fractographic observations, fracture surfaces from multiple regions of each tensile-tested specimen were examined for all composite compositions. Features such as particle fracture, matrix deformation, interfacial debonding, and void formation were consistently observed across the examined regions, confirming that the identified fracture mechanisms were not localized artifacts. The SEM micrographs presented in this study correspond to typical regions that reliably reflect the dominant fracture behavior of the Al6082/Al 2 SiO 5 /Al 2 O 3  hybrid composites.

It should be noted that the discussion on non-uniform particle distribution and its influence on crack propagation is based on qualitative observations from the available SEM micrographs and indirect indicators such as density reduction and mechanical property trends at higher reinforcement contents. While localized particle clustering was inferred from fracture surface features and porosity-related density variations, a dedicated quantitative analysis of particle distribution—such as high-resolution SEM/BSE imaging or elemental mapping—was not performed in the present study. Nevertheless, the observed behavior is consistent with well-established reports on stir-cast aluminum MMCs at elevated particle loadings, where increased clustering and porosity adversely affect crack paths and mechanical performance.

sections.heading: High Cycle Fatigue Test, Numerical Simulation, and Fractographic Investigation
paragraphs:
Table  6  presents the number of cycles to failure of the Al6082/Al 2 SiO 5 /Al 2 O 3  hybrid composite system for various combinations of Al 2 O 3  weight fraction, stirring rate, and stirring time. The fatigue tests were conducted under cyclic loading with maximum and minimum loads of 7.29 kN and 0.729 kN, respectively, at a frequency of 25 Hz. In the present study, the weight percentage of Al 2 SiO 5  particles is set to 5 wt.% for all cases from B1 to B9.

From Table  6 , it can be observed that the number of cycles to failure of the hybrid composite increases with the weight percentage Al 2 O 3  particles as it increases from 5 wt.% to 15 wt.%. In accordance with the observations for Al6082/Al 2 SiO 5 /B 4 C hybrid composite system reported in literature (Ref  42 ,  43 ), the fatigue life of the presently proposed Al6082/Al 2 SiO 5 /Al 2 O 3  hybrid composite system reaches 10 7  cycles, which is generally considered the run-out cycle or condition for infinite fatigue life. The B7 hybrid composite sample had the most failure cycles (11135826), while the B1 hybrid composite specimen showed the fewest failure cycles (7219263). Increasing the content of Al 2 O 3  particles had a positive effect on the fatigue performance of hybrid composite samples. Low fatigue potential for composites with 5 wt.% content of Al 2 O 3  particles can be attributed to various factors such as processing defects, reinforcement groups, and low surface area with stress concentration area. Most importantly, the main factor affecting the fatigue life of these specimens is the microstrains produced during hardening. The presence of such cast-related defects can be a potential site for early fatigue initiation, and the number of cycles due to failure is reduced in this hybrid composite system with 5 wt.% Al 2 O 3  particle content. In addition to this potential, if the processing conditions are not favorable, there is a high possibility of agglomeration of Al 2 O 3  particles (Ref  44 ,  45 ). Because Al 2 O 3  particles form clusters, they tend to bond easily, and the content of these individual particles does not have interfacial bond failure for the hybrid composite sample (5 wt.%). On the other hand, increasing the number of Al 2 O 3  particles increases the fatigue life of the hybrid composite, which is caused by the cracking of hard Al 2 O 3  particles (Ref  46 ).

Numerical analysis results of maximum principal stresses and fatigue life in Al6082/Al 2 SiO 5 /Al 2 O 3  hybrid composite systems for different material and process combinations are shown in Fig.  8 . The stress analysis is conducted by utilizing fatigue specimen geometry. The finite element model was developed using three-dimensional hexahedral solid elements, with a mesh convergence study guiding the selection of an average element size of approximately 0.5 mm in the gauge and high-stress regions, while coarser elements were employed elsewhere to optimize computational efficiency. From Fig.  8 (a), it can be seen that most of the stress is concentrated in the cross section of the fatigue specimen. The number of failure cycles is approximately 7541617 for specimens B1 to B3, 8941206 for specimens B4 to B6, and 10790981 for specimens B7 to B9 (refer Fig.  9 (b), (c) and (d)). The number of cycles to failure is obtained from the numerical analysis within the range of values obtained from the experiments. Fig. 9 Stress and fatigue life plot of Al6082/Al 2 SiO 5 /Al 2 O 3  hybrid composite system (a) Stress plot, (b) B1 to B3, (c) B4 to B6, (d) B7 to B9

Fatigue fracture surface of Al6082/Al 2 SiO 5 /Al 2 O 3  hybrid composite system for different specimen combinations is presented in Fig.  10 . It is observed from the micrograph that the micro-compression pores in the specimen appear to be the main reason for the failure of the composite specimen (Fig.  10 (a)-(f)). During fatigue testing the application of load leads to initiation of crack and leading to failure of composite sample. But it is important to note that the initiation of crack takes place at the micro-shrinkage pores very quickly than any other microstructure heterogeneities. Formation of such micro-shrinkage pores takes place during solidification due to different freezing temperatures of aluminum and its alloying elements. Along with pore size, the location of pores also plays important role as the pores near casting surfaces cause more stress concentration than that those present inside the casting (Ref  47 ). Overall, the presence of micro-shrinkage pores is known to have detrimental effect on the fatigue life of hybrid composites. Irrespective of the composite system, the failure can be attributed to the micro-shrinkage pores which are known to be formed during casting of Al6082 alloy and its hybrid composite systems. Fig. 10 Fatigue failure analysis of Al6082/Al 2 SiO 5 /Al 2 O 3  hybrid composite system with (a, b) 5%, (c, d) 10%, and (e, f) 15% Al 2 O 3  content

sections.heading: Fatigue Crack Propagation Test and Fractographic Investigation
paragraphs:
Table  7  shows the fatigue fracture crack propagation value for the Al6082/Al 2 SiO 5 /Al 2 O 3  hybrid composite system under different specimen combinations. From Table  7 , it can be seen that the fatigue fracture resistance increases with increasing particles Al 2 O 3 . The main reason for the increased fatigue resistance in hybrid composites with a higher content of Al 2 O 3  particles is that these particles act as an effective barrier to fatigue crack growth. This result also supports the work done by Gasem and others (Ref  48 ,  49 - 50 ) in the study of fatigue growth in Al6061/Al 2 O 3  composites. An increase in the volume fraction of reinforcement from 10% to 20% resulted in a decrease in the fracture toughness of Al6061 composites. Similarly, due to the presence of Al 2 O 3  particles now, the fatigue cracks around the particles and the direction of fatigue propagation are completely changed. Due to the strong interfacial bonding strength between the Al 2 O 3  particles and the Al6082 matrix, there is a possibility of particle fracture due to fatigue. Therefore, cracks tend to grow around Al 2 O 3  particles, and localized non-uniformity in particle distribution, as qualitatively observed, can contribute to weakening of the crack path (Table  8 ). This is the reason why the number of failed cycles for the hybrid composite with high Al 2 O 3  particle content (15%) is higher than for the hybrid composite with low Al 2 O 3  particle content (5%).

Figure  11  presents the numerical analysis of the Al6082/Al 2 SiO 5 /Al 2 O 3  hybrid composite system for different Al 2 O 3  weight fractions. The analysis was initiated with an initial crack length of 15.1 mm and allowed to propagate up to a final half-crack length of 22.85 mm. As shown in Fig.  11 (a)-(c), the predicted number of cycles to failure is approximately 8,381,978 for specimens B1-B3, 11,449,658 for specimens B4-B6, and 11,449,649 for specimens B7-B9. An increase in fatigue life is observed up to 10 wt.% Al 2 O 3 , as indicated by the percentage of required cycle weight. However, beyond 10  wt.% Al 2 O 3 , the fracture propagation life remains comparable to that at 10 wt.% Al 2 O 3 , suggesting no significant improvement in fracture toughness. Furthermore, the numerically predicted cycles to failure show good agreement with the experimental results. Fig. 11 Fatigue crack growth analysis from Al6082/Al 2 SiO 5 /Al 2 O 3  hybrid composite system (a) 5%, (b) 10%, (c) 15%

Crack propagation test fracture surfaces of Al6082/Al 2 SiO 5 /Al 2 O 3  hybrid composite system were analyzed under different parametric combinations as shown in Fig.  12 . From the micrographs, it is clear that the micro-shrinking pores in all samples are the chief contributors toward failure. During fatigue crack propagation tests, load application results in crack initiation in micro-compression holes. However, it should be noted that the initiation of cracking occurs faster in micro-compression pores than in other microstructures of homogeneity. Cracks grow along the micro-compression pore network, which is clearly seen from Fig.  12 (a) and (c) for 5% and 15% Al 2 O 3  particles-reinforced hybrid composite. However, the observation on the fracture surface does not show any particle separation due to the good interfacial bond strength between the Al 2 O 3  particles and the Al6082 matrix. In general, the presence of micro-shrink pores is known to have a detrimental effect on it. sections.heading: Conclusions
paragraphs: The present work investigated the effects of dual ceramic reinforcements and stir-casting process parameters on the microstructure, density, and mechanical behavior of Al6082/Al 2 SiO 5 /Al 2 O 3  hybrid metal matrix composites under monotonic and cyclic loading conditions. The hybrid composite system exhibited a maximum tensile strength of approximately 198 N/mm 2  for a composition containing 5 wt.% Al 2 SiO 5  and an intermediate Al 2 O 3  content under optimized stirring conditions. Microstructural and fractographic analyses revealed that the improvement in tensile strength was primarily attributed to grain refinement, increased dislocation density, and effective load transfer resulting from uniform dispersion and strong interfacial bonding between the reinforcements and the Al6082 matrix.

Density measurements showed only marginal increases with increasing reinforcement content, which were influenced by the higher density of ceramic particulates and the presence of micro-shrinkage porosity formed during solidification. The fatigue and fatigue crack propagation behavior of the hybrid composites improved with increasing Al 2 O 3  content, with composites containing 10-15 wt.% Al 2 O 3  exhibiting fatigue lives in the range of 8.4 × 10 6  to 1.11 × 10 7  cycles. Fractographic examination under cyclic loading conditions indicated that micro-shrinkage pores acted as the primary crack initiation sites, while the ceramic reinforcements contributed to crack deflection and delayed crack propagation. Overall, the study establishes clear relationships between reinforcement content, processing parameters, and mechanical performance of Al6082 hybrid MMCs, demonstrating their potential for structural applications requiring enhanced tensile strength and fatigue resistance.
